tickets.subject: Webhook not receiving SMS inbound events
tickets.body: Hi, we configured our messaging service webhook URL to point to https://our-app.example.com/sms/inbound but we are not receiving any POST requests when customers send SMS to our Twilio number. We verified the endpoint is publicly accessible and returns 200. We also checked our Twilio console and the messaging service shows the correct URL. This started happening yesterday around 3pm UTC. Our number is +15551234567. Can you help?

tickets.subject: Charged for calls we never made
tickets.body: We noticed on our invoice for last month there are over 4,000 outbound voice minutes billed to our account. We are a small team and only use the voice API for inbound calls. We have never initiated outbound calls programmatically. The charges total around $380 and appeared on the invoice dated the 1st of this month. Account SID is ACxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx. Please investigate and issue a refund.

tickets.subject: Flex agent UI keeps crashing when accepting a task
tickets.body: Critical issue affecting our entire contact center. When an agent clicks the Accept button on an incoming voice task in the Flex UI, the React component throws an uncaught exception and the whole browser tab crashes. This is happening across Chrome 124 and Edge 124 for all 47 of our agents. Error in console: 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading channel)'. We are on Flex UI version 2.7.1. This started after we deployed a plugin update last night. We are completely unable to handle customer calls right now.

tickets.subject: How do I set up SSO with Okta for Flex?
tickets.body: Hello, we want our agents to log into Flex using their existing Okta credentials instead of separate Twilio usernames. Can you walk me through how to configure SAML 2.0 SSO with Okta as the identity provider? I found some docs but they mention both the Flex SSO settings and something about OAuth in the console and I'm not sure which path to take. We are currently on Flex UI 2.x. Thank you.

tickets.subject: TwiML <Gather> verb not capturing DTMF input correctly
tickets.body: We have a TwiML application where we use the Gather verb to collect a 4-digit PIN from callers. Sometimes the gathered digits are truncated or empty even when the caller definitely pressed keys. Our TwiML looks like: <Gather numDigits='4' action='/verify-pin' method='POST'><Say>Please enter your PIN</Say></Gather>. We are seeing this on roughly 15% of calls. It seems worse on calls from mobile carriers. Is this a known issue or is there something wrong with our TwiML?

tickets.subject: Need help understanding our bill - lots of line items I don't recognize
tickets.body: Hi there, I've been looking at our bill and honestly I'm confused. There's a line for 'Programmable Messaging - Carrier Surcharge' which I don't remember agreeing to, and also something called 'Short Code MMS' which we don't use short codes at all. We only have a 10DLC long code number. And then there's a separate charge under Voice that says 'Insights' - what is that? I feel like we're being overcharged but I'm not sure. Can someone look at our account and explain what each of these charges are? Account SID starts with AC44...

tickets.subject: Feature request: ability to pause/resume task routing in Flex without going unavailable
tickets.body: Our supervisors have requested a way to temporarily stop new tasks from being routed to a specific agent - for example during a coaching session - without forcing the agent to change their activity state to Unavailable, which would affect our adherence reporting. Ideally this would be a supervisor action from the Teams View panel. Currently we have to use the TaskRouter Worker Activity API as a workaround which is clunky and shows up incorrectly in our WFM reports. Is this on the roadmap?

tickets.subject: SMS messages delivering with up to 45 minute delay
tickets.body: This is urgent for us. Starting this morning at approximately 9am EST our customers are reporting that appointment reminder SMS messages are arriving 30-45 minutes after we send them via the API. The API call returns a 200 with status 'queued' immediately but the messages sit in that state for a very long time. We send about 2,000 messages per hour during our morning batch. Our Messaging Service SID is MGxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx. Is there a platform incident? We don't see anything on the status page.

tickets.subject: OAuth token refresh failing with 401 in Flex plugin
tickets.body: We built a Flex plugin that calls our internal CRM API using an OAuth 2.0 access token stored in the Flex manager. The initial token works fine but when the token expires (1 hour) and we try to refresh it using the refresh_token grant, we get a 401 Unauthorized back from our token endpoint. We've confirmed the refresh token itself is valid when tested via Postman. The plugin uses FlexManager.getInstance().store to persist the tokens. We think something about how Flex handles the plugin lifecycle might be invalidating stored state but we're not sure. Could this be a Flex bug or is it our implementation?

tickets.subject: How to route calls to different queues based on caller ID?
tickets.body: Hi, we are building an IVR and want to route callers to different TaskRouter queues depending on their phone number - specifically we have a list of VIP customer numbers that should go straight to a premium support queue bypassing the normal queue. I know this involves TaskRouter workflows but I'm not sure how to pass the caller's number as a task attribute and then write the workflow filter expression to match against our VIP list. Do we maintain the list in TaskRouter or in our own database? What's the recommended architecture here?

tickets.subject: Account suspended - please help
tickets.body: Our account has been suspended and we can't send any messages or make calls. We received an email this morning but it was vague. We are in the middle of a product launch and this is a catastrophic situation for our business. We need this resolved TODAY. Nothing about our usage has changed. We process medical appointment reminders for clinics and have done so for 2 years without issues. Account SID is ACyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy.

tickets.subject: Flex WrapUp timer not auto-advancing to next state
tickets.body: Hey team, so we have this problem that's been going on for maybe two weeks now and I keep meaning to write in about it. Basically our agents finish a call and they go into the WrapUp activity which is great, but the thing is we set up the auto-wrap timeout to be 60 seconds in the Flex configuration, at least I think we did, and some agents are staying in WrapUp forever basically. It's not all agents, maybe like a third of them? And it seems like it might be related to whether they took a transfer at some point during the call but honestly I'm not sure. Also separately the supervisor dashboard shows some agents as Available when they're actually on a call but that might be a different thing. Anyway let me know what you think.

tickets.subject: Verify API: sending OTP but users never receive the code
tickets.body: We integrated the Twilio Verify API to send OTP codes for user login. The API returns a 'pending' status when we create the verification, which we understand means it was accepted, but a significant portion of our users (we estimate 20-30%) report never receiving the SMS. We are NOT using a custom template. This seems to affect users on certain carriers more than others - we've noticed AT&T users have more complaints. Our Verify Service SID is VAxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx. Is there a deliverability issue with Verify specifically or could this be a 10DLC registration problem?

tickets.subject: Feature request: dark mode for Flex agent desktop
tickets.body: A lot of our agents work overnight shifts and have been requesting a dark mode option for the Flex UI. Staring at a bright white screen for 8 hours causes eye strain. We know we can customize the theme via the Flex UI theming API in a plugin but implementing a full dark theme from scratch is a significant undertaking. It would be great if Twilio provided an official dark theme or a theme switcher out of the box. Is this planned?

tickets.subject: Programmable Voice: conference recording not starting
tickets.body: We use the <Conference> TwiML verb with record='record-from-start' but recordings are not being created. The conference connects fine, all participants can hear each other, but when the call ends we see no recording in the console and the RecordingStatusCallback URL we specified is never hit. We tested this with a simple TwiML Bin to rule out our application code and the same thing happens. Our account is a paid account with recordings enabled. Account SID is AC55...

tickets.subject: How do I migrate from Twilio Client JS SDK v1 to v2?
tickets.body: We have a fairly large legacy codebase using Twilio Client JS 1.x for browser-based calling. We want to upgrade to the Voice SDK 2.x. What are the key breaking changes we should be aware of? Specifically: (1) does the new SDK still use AccessTokens with the same structure, (2) is the Device.connect() API signature the same, (3) how do we handle the new audio constraints APIs? Also is there a coexistence period where we can run both versions or do we need a hard cutover? We have about 200 concurrent users so we need to plan this carefully.

tickets.subject: TaskRouter worker not going offline when browser tab closes
tickets.body: When an agent closes the browser tab or their browser crashes, their TaskRouter worker remains in the Available activity state. This means new tasks keep routing to them and then timeout after the reservation TTL, which impacts our queue SLA metrics. We have the Flex UI handling the worker state. We expected it would use the beforeunload event to set the worker offline but apparently this is not reliable. Is there a recommended way to handle this? Does Flex have a built-in heartbeat mechanism that will eventually mark the worker offline?

tickets.subject: Incorrect caller ID showing on outbound calls from Flex
tickets.body: When our agents make outbound calls from the Flex agent desktop, the caller ID showing to the recipient is not our main business number (+15559876543) as configured. Instead, some calls show a completely different Twilio number and some show 'Unknown'. This is confusing our customers who look up the number and don't recognize it as us. We set the callerId in the Flex Outbound Call configuration to our verified number. This is intermittent - roughly 1 in 10 calls has the wrong caller ID.

tickets.subject: Getting error 20003 on API requests after rotating API key
tickets.body: We rotated our Twilio API keys as part of a security audit last week. We updated the new API Key SID and Secret in our application's environment variables and redeployed. However we are now getting HTTP 401 errors with error code 20003 'Authentication Failed' on all REST API calls. We are using the Node.js Twilio helper library version 4.x. We double-checked the Key SID and Secret are correct by copying them fresh from the console. Account SID is also correct. The old key is definitely deactivated. What could cause this?

tickets.subject: 10DLC campaign registration rejected - not sure why
tickets.body: We submitted our 10DLC Campaign registration about 3 weeks ago and just got a rejection notification but the reason listed is just 'Content violation - see guidelines' which isn't very helpful. Our use case is sending order confirmation and shipping update messages to customers who have explicitly opted in at checkout. We are a registered LLC, our brand is verified, and we thought our message samples were compliant. Is the rejection coming from Twilio or from the carrier registry (TCR)? Can we resubmit and if so what should we change? We're losing money every day we can't send these messages.

tickets.subject: How do I stop Flex UI from losing agent activity state after accepting a task?
tickets.body:
Hi,

Wondering if there's something I'm missing in how activity transitions are supposed to work after task acceptance.

We're on Flex UI 2.7.1. I have a beforeAcceptTask override that does some lightweight attribute stamping on the worker before the task is accepted. Nothing heavy — just a worker.update call to set a couple of custom attributes.

The weird part: after the accept goes through, the agent's activity in the UI shows as Available but the TaskRouter side is showing them in Reserved. This only started happening after we deployed a new plugin version two nights ago. Agents are on Chrome 124.

So my question is basically — is there a recommended pattern for doing worker updates inside a beforeAcceptTask override, or is there ordering I need to respect so the UI and TaskRouter stay in sync?

I've tried looking at the console but nothing obvious jumps out. Status Report doesn't show anything I can clearly tie to this.

Thanks

gold.notes: bug implies issues is on Twilio's side which has not been confirmed yet. customer mentions deploying a new plugin.

tickets.subject: How do I properly configure wrap-up activity transitions so workers don't get stuck after reservation timeout?
tickets.body:
Hey Twilio support team,

I'm hoping someone can help me understand if I'm setting something up wrong, or point me to documentation I might be missing, because I've been going in circles on this for a few days now and I'm not sure if it's a configuration gap on my end or something else.

Some context: I'm a solo dev maintaining a Flex 2.7.1 deployment, running the standard Flex UI on Chrome 124. We have a fairly simple voice workflow — nothing too exotic. Workers sit in Available, get a reservation, and if they don't accept within our configured timeout window, the reservation times out and the task gets re-evaluated (I can see `task_re_evaluated_reason: reservation_timeout` in the TaskRouter logs, so that part is working as expected).

The thing I'm trying to understand is: after a reservation timeout fires, is there a correct way to make sure the worker automatically transitions to a specific Activity? Because what I'm observing is that the worker stays in Available (Activity SID `WA3f8b2c19d4e05a1b67890abcdef1234`) after the timeout, which is actually what we want in most cases — but then sometimes, seemingly at random, the worker gets pushed into an Unavailable state instead (Activity SID `WAc7d92e0f1a2b3456789012345678abcd`), and they have to manually click back to Available to receive tasks again.

I initially thought this might be related to our `DequeuePostWorkActivitySid` setting, but the timeouts I'm describing happen before the task is ever accepted, so post-work wrap-up shouldn't even be in play here, right? Like the worker never entered wrap-up, the reservation just timed out.

Here's what I've been doing to try to reproduce it consistently:
1. Worker logs in, goes Available — Workspace is `WS4a1b2c3d4e5f6789012345678901abcd`
2. A voice task comes in, reservation `WR9z8y7x6w5v4u3t2s1r0q9p8o7n6m5l` is created
3. Worker does NOT accept — just lets it sit past the timeout threshold
4. TaskRouter logs show the reservation timeout and task re-evaluation, as expected
5. Worker's activity in the TaskRouter Worker page flips to Unavailable — worker SID is `WK2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7`

Step 5 is what I don't understand. I haven't set any listener or action that should be pushing the worker to Unavailable on a reservation timeout. I've checked our plugins and we don't have any `reservation.timeout` handler calling `worker.update({ActivitySid: …})` for the Unavailable SID. Our plugin code only touches the `beforeAcceptTask` override for some logging.

Is there a built-in Flex or TaskRouter behavior where a reservation timeout automatically moves the worker to a fallback activity? And if so, is there somewhere I configure which activity that should be? I've read through the TaskRouter Worker Activity docs and the Flex wrap-up docs but I can't find anything that explicitly describes this behavior happening on timeout rather than on task completion.

I'd also just like to confirm: is this expected to be deterministic? Because the part that really puzzles me is that it doesn't happen every time. Maybe 30-40% of timeout events result in the worker going Unavailable. The other 60-70% the worker stays Available just fine. If this were a config option I'd set, I'd expect it to happen 100% of the time.

I've looked at the Status Report download from the Flex UI and I don't see any 45600 or 45601 errors logged around the time these transitions happen, so it doesn't seem like a plugin crash is causing a side effect. Checked `Flex.Monitor.getErrors()` output too and nothing stands out.

Any guidance on what's happening here and what knob I should be turning would be really appreciated. Happy to provide more logs or SIDs if needed.

Thanks so much

gold.notes: this appears to point to the agent offline activity setting which can set an agent to offline/unavailable if a reservation is missed.

tickets.subject: How do I stop plugins from crashing on second task accept?
tickets.body:
Hi — trying to figure out if we're missing some setup step or if there's a known workaround for this.

We have a small contact center (~15 agents) on Flex UI 2.7.1, Chrome 124. We deployed a new plugin version last Tuesday via a release (configuration SID FJxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx). The plugin adds a beforeAcceptTask override to pre-populate some task attributes before the agent clicks Accept.

Everything looks fine on the FIRST task each session. But on the second task acceptance in the same browser session, the override throws and the task never accepts. Agents see the reservation sit there until it times out. Console shows:

  Uncaught (in promise): FlexError [45601] Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'channel')

It's coming from our beforeAcceptTask handler. The weird part: if the agent refreshes the page, the first accept on that fresh session works fine again. Second one fails. Repeat.

Repro:
1. Log in as any agent (Worker WKxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx, tested across 3 workers)
2. Accept first inbound voice task — works, task picks up correctly
3. Complete task, go through wrap-up
4. Second reservation is created (WRxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx) — agent clicks Accept
5. FlexError 45601 thrown, task never accepts, reservation eventually times out

We checked Flex.Monitor.getErrors() after step 5 — the error is logged there. We also pulled a Status Report and the error appears consistently referencing our plugin's beforeAcceptTask callback.

Is there a recommended pattern for safely reading task channel data inside beforeAcceptTask across multiple task lifecycles in the same session? Wondering if we need to re-initialize something between tasks. Or is there a way to check whether the channel reference is still valid before we try to read it?

Happy to share the Status Report if that helps. TaskQueue is WQxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx, Workflow WWxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx.

Thanks

gold.notes: this pattern is repeatable for any agent logging in, so would have a higher business impact

tickets.subject: How do I prevent beforeAcceptTask from silently dropping the action on second attempt?
tickets.body:
Hi Twilio Support,

We're running Flex UI 2.7.1 with a custom plugin (let's call it TaskAcceptPlugin) deployed in our current active release. I wanted to check whether there's a recommended pattern for retrying a failed beforeAcceptTask override, because we're seeing some confusing behavior that I'm not sure is expected.

Here's the setup: in our plugin we register a beforeAcceptTask handler that makes a short fetch call to our internal API to log some metadata before the task is accepted. Most of the time this works fine. The issue appears when that fetch call fails with a network hiccup — our code catches the error and displays a toast to the agent, then returns without calling the `payload.reject()` callback explicitly (we assumed not calling reject would let the action fall through or allow a retry).

What actually happens:
1. Agent receives a reservation (WR4xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx, TaskQueue WQbxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx).
2. The agent clicks Accept.
3. The fetch to our API fails; we catch it and show the toast.
4. The AcceptTask action appears to silently swallow — no FlexError is surfaced, the Flex console shows no 45600/45601 code, and the reservation just sits in a pending state on the UI.
5. If the agent clicks Accept a second time, nothing happens at all — the button becomes unresponsive. The reservation eventually times out and the task gets re-evaluated.

We verified via `Flex.Monitor.getErrors()` immediately after the second click and it returns an empty array, which is what's confusing us — we would have expected a FlexError to appear there if the action framework was rejecting internally.

Repro steps (consistent across Chrome 124 and Edge 124):
- Simulate a network failure on the fetch inside beforeAcceptTask by blocking the URL in DevTools.
- Click Accept on an inbound voice task.
- Observe toast fires, but action appears to hang.
- Click Accept again.
- Button does nothing; no error logged to Flex Monitor.

Worker SID for our test agent: WK3xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx. I can also share the configuration SID for the release if that helps — just let me know.

So my questions are:
1. Is there a supported way to 'reset' the AcceptTask action so the agent can retry after a beforeAcceptTask failure?
2. Is it expected that a beforeAcceptTask handler that neither resolves cleanly nor calls reject would leave the action framework in a stuck state like this?

It's causing us moderate pain because affected agents have to refresh their entire Flex tab to get the reservation back, and by then the reservation has often timed out. We're happy to add explicit reject/resolve handling if that's the fix, but wanted to confirm first whether this stuck-state behavior on the second click is intentional or something we should escalate.

Thanks in advance for any guidance.

gold.notes: this pattern is repeatable for any agent logging in, so would have a higher business impact

tickets.subject: How do I stop workers from getting stuck in Reserved activity after reservation timeout?
tickets.body:
Hi,

We're running Flex UI 2.7.1 and have noticed something odd with our TaskRouter workers after reservation timeouts. Wondering if there's a config option I'm missing.

Situation: when a reservation times out (we have a 30s timeout set on the workflow), the task correctly gets re-evaluated (we see `task_re_evaluated_reason: reservation_timeout` in the event logs), but the worker remains in the Reserved activity indefinitely instead of transitioning back to Available or Unavailable. The agent's desktop shows them as Reserved with no active task, and they stop receiving new reservations. Only fix right now is the supervisor manually updating the worker's activity via the console.

Is there a specific `DequeuePostWorkActivitySid` we should be setting, or a workflow config option that handles the worker activity transition on timeout specifically?

Relevant details:
- Workspace: WSxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
- Affected workers: WKa1b2c3d4e5f6... (multiple, reproducible across agents)
- Workflow: WWxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
- Reservation SIDs at time of issue: WRxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx, WRxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
- Activity SIDs: Available = WAxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx, Reserved = WAxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
- No custom `reservation.timeout` handler in our plugin — we're relying on default behavior
- Repro: 1) worker in Available, 2) task assigned (enters Reserved), 3) worker doesn't accept within 30s, 4) reservation times out, 5) worker stays stuck in Reserved

We checked the TaskRouter.js worker events and we do see `reservation.timeout` fire, but no subsequent `activity.update` event ever comes through for the worker.

Chrome 124, no console errors, no 45600/45601 codes. Happens on both Chrome and Edge.

Is there a setting we need to enable, or a webhook we need to handle ourselves to push the worker back to a sane activity state after timeout?

Thanks

tickets.subject: How do I stop our plugin from crashing the desktop after deploying a new version?
tickets.body:
Hi Twilio support,

We're a small team running Flex 2.7.1 and we've been building out a custom plugin that we deploy through the Flex Plugins CLI. Things have been working pretty well overall, but we've run into a pattern we don't fully understand and wanted to ask if we're doing something wrong before assuming it's a problem on your end.

Whenever we cut a new plugin version and push it out through a new Release, our agents on Chrome 124 start seeing a broken desktop — the UI loads but several panels are blank and they can't accept tasks. It clears up if we close and reopen the browser tab sometimes, but not reliably. We went ahead and rolled back to a prior configuration by releasing the older configuration SID and that fixed everyone immediately, so we know our new plugin version is involved somehow.

Here's the part we're confused about: we've now reproduced this twice across two separate plugin versions that looked fine in our staging environment. Both times, the desktop breaks for all agents at once right after the release goes live. When we check the browser console there's a reference to something being undefined relating to a channel property, but we haven't been able to trace it back to a specific line in our plugin code.

Our questions are basically:
1. Is there a recommended way to test a plugin version against a production-like environment before it affects all agents?
2. Is the Status Report tool the right place to start diagnosing what's happening during initialization, or is there something more specific we should be capturing?
3. Could the issue be that our plugin is running some initialization logic before certain Flex SDKs are fully ready, and if so, is there a safe event or lifecycle hook we should be waiting on?

We're not in a rush but this is starting to slow down our deploys since we have to roll back every time. Happy to provide our account details or any other information if it helps.

Thanks so much.

gold.notes: mistake... I see they say customer says they are not in a rush

tickets.subject: How do we prevent beforeAcceptTask from occasionally blocking agents?
tickets.body:
Hi,

We're running Flex UI 2.7.1 across a large agent population (Chrome 124). We added a beforeAcceptTask override in our plugin a few weeks ago to do some pre-acceptance attribute stamping before a task is accepted.

General question: is there a recommended pattern for invoking a follow-up action inside a beforeAcceptTask override? We're currently calling Flex.Actions.invokeAction inside the override and returning the result.

The reason we're asking: intermittently, maybe 5-10 times a day out of hundreds of acceptances, the task acceptance just silently stops. The agent sees the reservation ring, nothing happens when they click Accept, and the task eventually times out and goes back into the queue. It doesn't happen to any specific agent or queue. No visible error in the UI on the agent's screen, and it's not consistent enough that we can reliably reproduce it on demand.

We noticed if we temporarily remove our beforeAcceptTask override entirely, we stop seeing the stuck acceptances. So we suspect something about how we have it wired up is occasionally causing the action chain to not complete, but we're not sure what the correct way to structure this is.

Workspace is WS redacted, TaskQueue in question is WQ redacted. Happy to pull a Status Report from an affected agent session if that helps.

What's the right approach here?

gold.notes: the fact that it is intermittent points to a config setting needing to be increased
